subject.title: Feature: Respect userTimezone in memory file timestamps and naming

question: Should bundled `session-memory` filenames, fallback HHMM slugs, and `# Session` headers use `agents.defaults.userTimezone` instead of the gateway host or `TZ` local timezone?
rationale: Current shipped docs and behavior say host local date for the hook, while pre-compaction memory flush already follows configured `userTimezone`; aligning them changes a user-visible artifact naming contract.

options.title: Adopt `userTimezone` for session-memory
options.body: Use the existing configured-timezone helpers for the hook filename date, fallback slug, and header, with focused docs/tests and no new config key.

options.title: Keep host-local hook behavior
options.body: Leave the shipped host-local contract in place and clarify that this hook intentionally follows the gateway host or `TZ`, not `agents.defaults.userTimezone`.

options.title: Add a dedicated memory timezone
options.body: Introduce a separate memory artifact timezone only if maintainers want memory output decoupled from `userTimezone`, accepting the schema/docs/upgrade cost.

recommendation.title: Adopt `userTimezone` for session-memory
recommendation.body: Use the existing configured-timezone helpers for the hook filename date, fallback slug, and header, with focused docs/tests and no new config key.

likelyOwner.reason: This account merged the current host-local session-memory behavior and is the clearest routing candidate for deciding whether to expand that contract.
